senses: A single unit combining transmission gearbox, clutch, final drive, and differential.
Below the conjunctiva.
One who swallows packets of drugs in order to smuggle them.
Any fish of the family Chiasmodontidae.
A priest or priestess of the traditional Hawaiian religion.
Synonym of mirror ball.
examples: Six years later there were barely any dancehalls to supervise—it was all glitzy discos attached to pubs. Glitterballs. Lassies writhing on little checkerboard handkerchiefs of dancefloor.

senses: A bacterial toxin (usually an exotoxin) whose toxicity has been weakened or suppressed
Any of a variety of stuffed pastries found in Spanish, Filipino, and Latin American cuisine.
ety: Borrowed from Spanish empanada, past participle of empanar (“to wrap in bread”).

senses: Opium prepared for smoking.
Obtained by using a colorimeter.
A title bestowed by the king on certain nobles in the 15th-17th centuries, who granted them governorship of a province or charged them with conquering a foreign territory
ety: Borrowed from Spanish adelantado, from Spanish adelantar (“to advance, to promote”).

senses: Characterised by tweets (in various senses).
examples: If, though, he's curious about the voice of a particular instrument — “What made that high tweety sound?” — a knowledgeable parent can provide answers.

senses: The act of circumscribing or the quality of being circumscribed.
Anything that circumscribes or a circumscribed area.
An electoral district; used often in texts treating electoral systems in Romance countries.
One of a set of rows of tightly braided hair close to the scalp, forming a hairstyle, of African origin.
ety: From corn + row, reflecting the figurative evocation of rows of corn in a cornfield.
examples: The physician should evaluate for a history of tight ponytails, buns, chignons, braids, twists, weaves, cornrows, dreadlocks, sisterlocks, and hair wefts in addition to the usage of religious hair coverings.
Coolio, whose spindly and sprouting cornrows defined his look, went on to sell over 17 million records throughout his career.

senses: Synonym of Asian palm civet.
ety: Likely borrowed from Bengali বান্দর (bandor, “monkey”) or Hindi बंदर (bandar, “monkey”).

senses: Of fourth rank or order.
Of a mathematical expression containing e.g. x⁴.
ety: Derived from Latin quaternārius (“containing or consisting of four”), from quaternī (“four each”, “four at a time”) + -ārius (whence the English suffix -ary); compare the French quaternaire.

senses: A type of electronic mailing list, allowing for distribution of email to many subscribers.
examples: Rather than producing flashy television spots, it has placed simple ads on Web sites of news organizations and urbanbaby.com, and tried to spread its positions by posting on education and community listservs and blogs.

senses: The process or result of designing or presenting in accordance with a style. Adoption of a style.
Simplified representation; reduction to a pattern or conventional form; abstraction; decorative generalization.
examples: If you separate your work from reality, the artistry and stylization become the focus.

senses: To lift a ban against.
Registrar, clerk.
A professional who calculates financial values associated with uncertain events subject to risk, such as insurance premiums or pension contributions.
ety: From Latin āctuārius (“copyist, account-keeper”), from āctus (“public business”); see actuarius.

senses: Having to do with one's husband's brother.
ety: From Latin lēvir (“husband's brother, brother-in-law”) + -ate (adjective-forming suffix), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dayh₂wḗr (“one's brother-in-law”).

senses: A sturdy box with a lock, for storing valuables.
ety: From strong + box. Compare French coffre-fort.
examples: An inroad on the strongbox, or an erasure in the ledger, or a missummation in a fitted account, could hardly have surprised him more disagreeably.

senses: A measure of the degree to which a colloid is polydisperse
The spiritual power or wisdom that resides in holy places and people, especially in a Sufi.
Someone who uses a sickle; a sickleman; a reaper.
A medieval Arab condiment made from fermented barley.
ety: Borrowed from Arabic مُرِّيّ (murriyy), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܡܘܼܪܝܵܐ (mūryā, “brine”), borrowed from Latin muria (“brine, salty pickling solution”).

senses: A Buddhist ceremonial mace and symbol, usually interpreted as both a diamond and a thunderbolt.
One of the five central Buddhist principles, representing indestructible substance that cuts and penetrates through emotional instability or uncertainty.
The weapon of Indra, the god of heaven and the chief deity of the Rigvedic pantheon, used to kill sinners and ignorant persons.
ety: From Sanskrit वज्र (vájra). Doublet of waker; see there for more.
examples: At the centre is a five-pronged vajra draped and bound with a coloured silk scarf, representing one of the Five Buddha wisdoms or activities.
Those five principles or buddha families are called vajra, ratna, padma, karma, and buddha.

senses: Someone or something that moves, acts or thinks fast.
An alcoholic drink that is consumed quickly.
A small European and Asian passerine bird, Prunella modularis; the hedge sparrow or hedge warbler.
ety: From Middle English donek, dunok, from Old English *dunnuc, equivalent to dun (“brownish grey”) + -ock (diminutive suffix). Compare Old High German doniklīn (“hedge-sparrow; dunnock”). Compare ruddock.

senses: A medical doctor specializing in the eye: deficiencies of vision requiring correction, and diseases. Compare optometrist.
Someone to whom something is dedicated.
Consisting of three names or parts or terms.
The interconnected outer surface of a spore.
ety: From Latin tēctum (“roof”), from tegō (“to cover”), cognate with Ancient Greek τέγος (tégos, “roof; covered room”). Doublet of tect.

senses: The kissing gourami.
ety: Agent noun of kiss: from kiss + -er.

senses: The property of being configurable.
exhibiting sorrow; dejected; distraught; sad. (of a person)
Producing sorrow; causing grief.
ety: From Middle English sorweful, from Old English sorhful, sorgful (“full of care; anxious; sorrowful”), from Proto-Germanic *surgafullaz (“full of care; anxious”), equivalent to sorrow + -ful. Cognate with Old High German sorgfol (“careful; anxious”), Norwegian sorgfull (“sorrowful”), Icelandic sorgfullur (“lamentable”).

senses: Having an atypical neurological configuration.
ety: From neuro- + divergent. Coined by neurodiversity activist Kassiane Asasumasu in 2000.

senses: A large convex molding, typically semicircular in cross section, which commonly projects at the base of a column and above the plinth.
ety: Borrowed from Latin torus (“a round, swelling, elevation, protuberance”).

senses: A person who coats material with a fluid.
A machine that coats material with a fluid.
examples: The curtain coater broke down and the factory had to close temporarily.

senses: A person who opposes; especially a member of an official opposition
examples: They felt that the fellow was a quockerwodger rather than a politician, an againster rather than a true American, an oppositionist in fundamental things rather than a sincere patriot.
I see your marriage as a move to establish links with the oppositionist Russian intelligentsia.

senses: In harness racing, a horse with a gait in which the front and back legs on one side take a step together alternating with the legs on the other side; as opposed to a trotter.
A pacemaker (one who sets the pace in a race).
A timer in an electric toothbrush that indicates how long the user should spend brushing in each part of the mouth.
